annotations.title: Draw on my open Vela chart

description: Draws on the chart the signed-in member has open right now in Vela, at times and prices you give: horizontal levels, shaded zones, trendlines, projection paths with an arrowhead, channels, Fibonacci retracements, text notes, vertical time lines and long or short positions with a stop and a target. Use it to put a plan, a scenario or a target on the member's own chart; for levels and concepts the candles define (fair value gaps, liquidity, key levels and the like) use vela_mark_up_chart, which finds the exact prices itself. The drawings appear as real, labelled drawings in Vela's house style, the member watches them being drawn, and their own drawings are never touched. Give a drawing an explain and the member is walked through the drawings on their chart, your words in a bubble on each. Times are on the chart's clock ("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM", the clock vela_read_chart names), or ISO 8601 with an offset. It reads no prices: draw at prices the member gave or that a markup returned, never at guessed ones. Returns the group its drawings belong to, which vela_remove_drawings takes. With the member's Vela tab on screen it happens in front of them within seconds. When it is not (they are in another tab), the change is queued and applied the moment they look at Vela again, within 10 minutes: the result then says queued, so tell them to open Vela. Requires signing in with a LuxAlgo account (OAuth).

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

arrow.description: path, trendline: end in an arrowhead (a path does by default).

end_time.description: level: where it stops; position: where the box ends.

explain.description: One or two plain sentences on what this part is and why it matters here. With it, the member is walked through the parts on their chart, a bubble on each in turn with Next and Exit: use it whenever you are teaching or presenting an analysis.

extend.description: level, zone, trendline: run to the chart's right edge (a level does by default).

label.description: A short label shown on the drawing.

points.description: Anchor points, each a time and a price. level: 1 (where it starts); zone, fib, trendline: 2 corners; path: 2 to 12 vertices in order; channel: 4 (upper start, upper end, lower start, lower end); note: 1; position: 1 (the entry).

text.description: note: the text of the card; \n between lines.

tone.description: The colour role; Vela's house style picks the colour.

slot.description: One chart of a multi-chart layout, by position (0 is the top-left, in reading order). Leave it out for the chart the member is working on.

title.description: What this set of drawings is, e.g. "Bullish scenario to 2,920".

name: vela_draw_on_chart
